title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Student assignment data (work file, student id, course, submission timestamp) transmitted over network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to potential privacy breach of student information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without guaranteed encryption

title: Metadata Linking and Identification
description: Data flow metadata (timing, source/destination identifiers) could be used to link students to specific courses or activities, enabling profiling or tracking of student behavior.
assumptions: Network metadata is observable and potentially correlated with student activities

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Data
description: Grades Portal Web App may store student assignment data without adequate access controls, allowing unauthorized personnel to access student information.
assumptions: System has multiple users with varying access levels

title: Unintended Data Usage
description: Student data collected for assignment submission may be used for purposes beyond the stated educational purpose, such as marketing or data mining.
assumptions: System may have broader data usage policies than explicitly communicated

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Sharing
description: Student may not be fully aware of the implications of submitting data to the Grades Portal, including potential data retention, sharing, or misuse.
assumptions: Student may not have complete understanding of data handling practices

title: Sharing of student identifiers at source
description: The Grades Portal Web App shares student ID and requesting role with the Assignment & Grading Service, creating a risk that these identifiers could be misused or exposed inappropriately at the source element.
assumptions: Student IDs are unique identifiers for data subjects

title: Identifiers in transit
description: Student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role are transmitted in data flow DF2, creating data-centric privacy risks where metadata about the parties could be used to link or identify them during transit.
assumptions: Data in transit may be intercepted or monitored

title: Processing of identified data at destination
description: The Assignment & Grading Service processes student identifiers and role information, which could lead to inappropriate processing or storage of identified data without adequate safeguards.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading purposes

title: Non-repudiation of grading actions
description: The assignment of student ID and requesting role creates evidence that could be used to attribute grading actions to specific individuals, potentially preventing students from denying involvement in grading disputes.
assumptions: Grading actions are attributed to specific roles

title: Unintended data disclosure to third parties
description: The grading service may inadvertently disclose student assignment data to unauthorized third parties during the storage process, violating data minimality and privacy principles.

title: Data disclosed beyond necessary scope
description: The grading service may share more personal data (student id, course, submission time) than strictly required for the assignment storage function, violating data minimality.

title: Data linkability through metadata
description: Data in transit may contain metadata about the parties (student, course) that could be used to link or identify individuals, even if the content itself is not disclosed.

title: Data disclosed through storage access
description: The assignment store may disclose student data to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data retrieval mechanisms.

title: Data integrity compromised during storage
description: The assignment store may corrupt, tamper with, or lose the stored assignment data, affecting data availability and integrity.

title: Teacher's identity disclosed during login
description: When the teacher logs in to access the submission queue, their identity is revealed to the system and potentially to other users who can see their login status or profile information.
assumptions: Teacher's login credentials are used to identify them to the system

title: Teacher's location tracked through login
description: The teacher's login activity could be used to track their location or access patterns, potentially revealing when and where they access the system.
assumptions: System logs teacher login times and potentially IP addresses

title: Teacher's login credentials intercepted in transit
description: Teacher's login credentials transmitted from EE3 to P1 could be intercepted by malicious actors during data transmission, potentially leading to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Data flows over potentially insecure network connections

title: Teacher's identity inferred from login metadata
description: Meta-data about the login request (such as timing, frequency, or pattern) could be used to identify or link the teacher to specific courses or submissions.
assumptions: Login metadata is captured and potentially analyzed

title: Teacher's identity stored and potentially linked to submissions
description: The system stores teacher identity and links it to submission review activities, potentially enabling tracking of which teachers review which submissions.
assumptions: Teacher identity is stored in the system and associated with review activities

title: Teacher's review activity disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The system may disclose teacher's review activity or submission queue information to unauthorized parties, potentially revealing which courses or submissions teachers are reviewing.
assumptions: System may have inadequate access controls or data sharing policies

title: Lawful basis for student data sharing
description: Portal may share student data with teachers without proper legal basis, consent, or authorization as required by educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR).

title: Information sharing beyond necessity
description: Portal may share more student information than necessary for the intended purpose (e.g., submission times, metadata) which could enable tracking or profiling.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Portal may not comply with applicable data protection regulations regarding student data sharing, including proper documentation, audit trails, and data minimization principles.

title: Unintended use of student data
description: Teachers may use student data (names, work content, submission times) for purposes beyond the intended educational assessment, such as administrative tracking or external sharing.

title: Data in transit exposure
description: Student data transmitted from portal to teacher may be exposed to interception or unauthorized access during transmission, especially if not properly encrypted.

title: Unauthorized Teacher Access
description: Teacher (EE3) may not be properly authenticated or authorized to record grades, potentially allowing unauthorized individuals to access the system and record inappropriate grades.
assumptions: Teacher identity verification is required but may be weak or absent

title: Intentional Data Deception by Teacher
description: Teacher may intentionally enter false or misleading grades and feedback to manipulate student records or cover up inappropriate behavior.
assumptions: Teacher has incentive to manipulate data

title: Unintended Disclosure of Sensitive Information
description: Teacher may accidentally include sensitive student information (e.g., health conditions, disciplinary issues) in grade feedback that should remain private.
assumptions: Teacher may not be fully aware of privacy boundaries

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Grade data and feedback in transit between Teacher and Grades Portal Web App may be intercepted by unauthorized parties if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data transmission may occur over public or semi-public networks

title: Data Tampering During Transmission
description: Data in transit may be modified or tampered with by malicious actors, potentially altering grades or feedback before reaching the destination.
assumptions: No integrity protection mechanisms in place

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Grades
description: Grades Portal Web App may allow unauthorized users to access student grades and feedback without proper access controls.
assumptions: Access controls may be weak or absent

title: Unintended Disclosure of Student Information
description: Grades Portal Web App may inadvertently expose student information to unauthorized parties through data leaks, API misconfigurations, or improper data handling.
assumptions: System may have vulnerabilities in data handling

title: Unauthorized data disclosure at source
description: The grading service may share grade records with unauthorized recipients or without proper authorization controls, potentially exposing sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has appropriate access controls and authorization mechanisms in place.

title: Unauthorized access to data at source
description: The grading service may be accessed by unauthorized personnel who could improperly share or modify grade records before transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has appropriate access controls and authorization mechanisms in place.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Grade records in transit between the grading service and database could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network that may not be fully secured.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure at destination
description: The grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized personnel who could retrieve and disclose sensitive student grade information.
assumptions: Assumes the database has appropriate access controls and authorization mechanisms in place.

title: Unauthorized access to stored data
description: The grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized personnel who could improperly read or modify stored grade records.
assumptions: Assumes the database has appropriate access controls and authorization mechanisms in place.

title: Unauthorized access to grades
description: Student may not be properly authorized to access their own grades, potentially due to lack of identity verification or authentication controls at the source.
assumptions: Assumes student identity verification is performed before data sharing

title: Metadata exposure in transit
description: Data flow may contain metadata (e.g., timestamps, IP addresses, request patterns) that could be used to link or identify the student or other parties.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over network infrastructure

title: Inappropriate data disclosure
description: Grades Portal Web App may disclose student grades to unauthorized parties or inappropriately share data beyond the student's access scope.
assumptions: Assumes system has proper access controls and data sharing policies

title: Inappropriate identification of student data
description: System may process student data in a way that identifies or links the student to their grades beyond necessary scope.
assumptions: Assumes system has proper data minimization and anonymization controls

title: Inaccurate or outdated grades displayed
description: The portal may display grades or teacher feedback that are inaccurate, outdated, or misleading, potentially causing confusion or harm to the student.
assumptions: Assumes grades and feedback are stored in the system and displayed to students.

title: Insufficient notification of data display
description: The student may not be adequately informed about what data is being displayed, how it is being used, or the purposes for which it is being shared.
assumptions: Assumes standard notification practices may not be implemented for all data displays.

title: Unintended disclosure during transmission
description: Data in transit between the portal and student could potentially be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, especially if transmission is not properly secured.
assumptions: Assumes data flows over network connections that may be vulnerable to interception.

title: Non-compliant data sharing practices
description: The portal may not be fully compliant with applicable privacy regulations when displaying student data, potentially violating data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the portal operates under various privacy regulations that may not be fully addressed.

title: Parent shares unauthorized child data
description: Parent may request or share child's grades data beyond their legitimate authorization, potentially violating privacy boundaries between parent and child accounts.
assumptions: Parent account is linked to child account but parent may not have full access rights to all child data.

title: Parent unintentionally shares sensitive data
description: Parent may unintentionally share more child data than intended during login or data request, such as exposing additional personal information.
assumptions: Parent may not be fully aware of all data fields being shared during authentication or data retrieval.

title: Data interception during transit
description: Child's grades data in transit from parent to portal may be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Data flow may not be adequately encrypted or protected during transmission.

title: Data disclosure during transmission
description: Data in transit may be exposed to unauthorized observers, potentially revealing parent-child relationship or child's academic performance.
assumptions: Data flow may lack sufficient confidentiality protections during transmission.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child grades
description: Grades Portal may disclose child's grades to unauthorized parties, including parent's other accounts or third parties without proper authorization.
assumptions: Portal may not have adequate access controls to prevent unauthorized data disclosure.

title: Portal compromise leading to data exposure
description: Grades Portal may be compromised, leading to unauthorized access to parent's child data and grades information.
assumptions: Portal may have vulnerabilities that could be exploited by attackers.

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: The Grades Portal may expose student grades, feedback, and submission history to unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient or if the system is compromised.
assumptions: Assumes the portal has some access controls but they may not be robust enough to prevent all unauthorized access attempts.

title: Lawfulness of Data Sharing
description: The sharing of student grades and academic records with parents may not be fully lawful if proper consent mechanisms are not in place or if data sharing exceeds what is legally permitted.
assumptions: Assumes there may be gaps in consent documentation or legal compliance for data sharing with parents.

title: Data Minimization Violation
description: The portal may share more data than necessary for the stated purpose, including potentially sensitive information beyond what parents need to know about their child's academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes the portal shares comprehensive data without filtering based on necessity.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Student grades and academic records transmitted from the portal to parents may be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the data flow is not properly encrypted or secured.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may not have adequate encryption or security measures in place.

title: Parental Unauthorized Disclosure
description: Parents receiving the data may disclose student grades and academic records to unauthorized third parties, violating student privacy.
assumptions: Assumes parents may not be bound by strict confidentiality obligations regarding student data.

title: Data Retention Without Minimization
description: Parents may retain student grades and academic records beyond what is necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes parents may keep data longer than legally or ethically required.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing by Administrator
description: School Administrator may share sensitive student/parent data without proper authorization or in an insecure manner, potentially exposing confidential information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Administrator has access to create, modify, and disable accounts and parent-child links

title: Data Quality Issues from Administrator Input
description: Administrator may enter incorrect, incomplete, or inconsistent data when creating, modifying, or disabling accounts and parent-child links, affecting data integrity.
assumptions: Administrator is responsible for data entry and validation

title: Unauthorized Access to Processed Data
description: Grades Portal Web App may store and process sensitive student/parent data in a way that allows unauthorized access, potentially exposing confidential information.
assumptions: Web app stores account and relationship data

title: Unauthorized Data Deletion by Administrator
description: Administrator may delete or disable accounts and parent-child links without proper authorization or oversight, potentially causing data loss or privacy violations.
assumptions: Administrator has delete/disable capabilities

title: Unintended Privacy Consequences from Data Processing
description: Processing of parent-child links and account data may have unintended privacy consequences, such as revealing relationships or enabling profiling without consent.
assumptions: System processes relationship data for various purposes

title: Unauthorized data sharing
description: The grading service may share account records and parent-child relationship links without proper authorization or with insufficient access controls, potentially exposing data that should be restricted.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has legitimate access to account data but may lack proper authorization controls.

title: Data linkability through parent-child relationships
description: Parent-child relationship links in transit may be used to link or identify users, potentially enabling tracking or correlation of user activities across different contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the parent-child relationship data contains identifiable information that could be used for linking.

title: Data confidentiality at destination
description: The account directory may store account records and parent-child relationships in a way that exposes sensitive data to unauthorized access or breaches.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory may have insufficient security controls for storing sensitive account data.

title: Explicit disclosure of personal data to third-party cloud provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider as part of nightly backup and replication.

title: Data stored in third-party cloud provider jurisdiction
description: Personal data is stored on cloud hosting provider infrastructure, potentially in a different jurisdiction with different data protection laws.

title: Transfer of potentially unnecessary personal data
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory may include more personal data than strictly required for backup/replication purposes.

title: Data in transit potentially exposed
description: Data flows in transit between P2 and EE5 could be intercepted or monitored by third parties.

title: Grade records potentially linkable to students/parents/teachers
description: Grade records in the database may contain identifiers that can be linked to specific students, parents, or teachers, enabling identification of individuals based on their academic performance data.
assumptions: Assumes grade records contain or can be correlated with personal identifiers

title: Sensitive information potentially deducible from grade records
description: Grade records may allow deduction of sensitive information about students, such as learning disabilities, special education status, or behavioral issues, based on patterns in academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes grade records contain or can be correlated with special education or behavioral data

title: Data flow metadata potentially linkable to parties
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timestamps, volume, parties involved) could be used to link or identify the students, parents, and teachers whose grade records are being transferred.
assumptions: Assumes metadata about the data flow is captured and potentially analyzed

title: Processed grade data potentially linkable to individuals
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may process grade records in ways that create or enhance linkability to specific students, parents, and teachers, potentially enabling profiling or identification.
assumptions: Assumes the service processes data in ways that maintain or create identifiers

title: Unintended data processing for student/parent/teacher views
description: The service may process grade records to build views for multiple parties (students, parents, teachers) without proper consideration of consent or necessity for each party.
assumptions: Assumes multiple parties may have access to grade data without explicit consent
